messages.subject: Encoding problem between PC and Mac?
parts:

When we change the encoding to work on the Mac, it won’t run on the PC. Anyone have ideas?

Thanks!

messages.author: 4b16035cff9b0f8a
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Encoding problem between PC and Mac?
parts:
Encoding is a bane of existence when you're working cross-platform. Default encoding is UTF-8, which doesn't always play nice between unix and windows for Reasons.

Sadly, there is still no 100% solution that I'm aware of. Try explicitly writing and reading the files using latin-1 (ISO 8859-1) encoding (can't give exact methods because it varies by filetype, but it's usually something like write(foo, foo.file, encoding="latin-1"). 

That usually (but not always) works for me, assuming whatever you're working with is in english or another language that uses the latin character set.

Thanks,
Erica

--
Erica Rettig
Ph.D. Candidate
Graduate Group in Ecology, UC Davis

messages.author: 5f533b50135a7f86
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Encoding problem between PC and Mac?
parts:
Another thing to check would be the end-of-line characters.  There are three distinct ways to end a line (https://stackoverflow.com/a/18907200), and you can get weird behavior and errors if either (a) the reading function is expecting the wrong one or (b) the file uses different end-of-line characters on different lines, usually as a result of being previously processed on different operating systems.  

I once spent several hours figuring out that, like, my file had \n on even lines and \r on odd lines.  

Good luck, 
Dan
-----
Dan Hicks
Assistant Professor
Cognitive and Information Sciences
University of California, Merced

messages.subject: RE: [D-RUG]: Encoding problem between PC and Mac?
parts:
We recently ran into a problem in a GIS workshop and it ended up being curly quotes, like the variations of ‘ and “ and the direction they face. Good luck tracking down your offender!

 

Naomi

From: davi...@googlegroups.com [mailto:davi...@googlegroups.com] On Behalf Of Dan Hicks
Sent: Wednesday, December 11, 2019 1:39 PM
To: davi...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Encoding problem between PC and Mac?

 

Another thing to check would be the end-of-line characters.  There are three distinct ways to end a line (https://stackoverflow.com/a/18907200), and you can get weird behavior and errors if either (a) the reading function is expecting the wrong one or (b) the file uses different end-of-line characters on different lines, usually as a result of being previously processed on different operating systems.  

 

I once spent several hours figuring out that, like, my file had \n on even lines and \r on odd lines.  

 

Good luck, 

Dan

-----

Dan Hicks

Assistant Professor

Cognitive and Information Sciences

University of California, Merced

Pronouns: they/them/their



On Dec 11, 2019, at 1:26 PM, Ingrid Behrsin <iabe...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:

 

Gotcha - this is what we've tried, so it's good to hear we're not alone! We ended up just reading each of the files and are working on finding the offending character. Fingers crossed :).

 

On Wed, Dec 11, 2019 at 1:17 PM Erica Rettig <erica....@gmail.com> wrote:

Encoding is a bane of existence when you're working cross-platform. Default encoding is UTF-8, which doesn't always play nice between unix and windows for Reasons.

 

Sadly, there is still no 100% solution that I'm aware of. Try explicitly writing and reading the files using latin-1 (ISO 8859-1) encoding (can't give exact methods because it varies by filetype, but it's usually something like write(foo, foo.file, encoding="latin-1"). 

 

That usually (but not always) works for me, assuming whatever you're working with is in english or another language that uses the latin character set.


Thanks,
Erica

--
Erica Rettig
Ph.D. Candidate
Graduate Group in Ecology, UC Davis

Dan
